update.title: expand: Improve tuple-extraction handling.
update.body:
After the REGMODE_NATURAL_SIZE changes have landed, this is another small
improvement for PR125390 which also fixes aarch64's struct_3_256.c
regression.
Originally a riscv-specific issue and ICE, I noticed poor codegen when we
extract values from a tuple type.  In the optimized dump we have:

  vect_array.9 = .MASK_LEN_LOAD_LANES (&c, 32B, { -1, -1, -1, -1 }, _44(D), 4, 0);
  _48 = BIT_FIELD_REF <vect_array.9[0], 32, 96>;
  _50 = BIT_FIELD_REF <vect_array.9[1], 32, 96>;
  f_13 = _48 ^ _50;
  a = f_13;

and _48 as well as _50 spill to memory instead of extracting directly.

We end up with

  (subreg:RVVMF2SI (reg:RVVMF2x2SI 138 [ vect_array.9 ]) 0)

which, as we pun the with a large integer mode, involves OImode
that we cannot "move".  We might be able to work around that in the
target in unintuitive ways :)  and we could also offer vec_extract for
all tuple modes.  However, I figured it would be much easier if expand
already handled the tuple -> vector part for us so just a vector extract
is left for the target to do.

The patch adds multi-vector-reg -> vector functionality as a separate
function and also moves vector-vector, as well as vector-element extract into
new functions.

	PR middle-end/125390

update.title: RISC-V: Support ".option [no]exact" assembler directives
update.body:
This commit adds two assembler directives: ".option exact" and
".option noexact" (enable/disable the exact mode) as discussed in
<https://github.com/riscv-non-isa/riscv-asm-manual/pull/122> and
already implemented in LLVM.

When the exact mode is enabled,

1.  Linker relaxations are turned off,
2.  Instruction aliases that will change the encoding from the
    (likely non-alias) instruction with the same name are disabled
    (e.g. "addi" will never turn into "c.addi" even if optimizable) and
3.  Assembler relaxation of branch instructions are disabled
    (e.g. "blt" with a long offset will not turn into "bge + j").

Macros like "li" (known to be expanded into possibly complex sequences)
may still expand to complex instruction sequences but at least each
instruction emitted by macros is still subject to the behavior above.

Currently, interactions between ".option relax/norelax" and
".option exact/noexact" are designed to be LLVM-compatible (i.e.
".option exact/noexact" imply ".option norelax/relax", respectively)
but considered flaky and strongly discouraged from using both.

cf. <https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/122483>

update.title: PR rtl-optimization/123905 - Failure to optimize away sign extension on RISC-V
update.body:
This patch fixes PR123905, where the compiler generates redundant sign
extensions and bit masks on RISC-V when using __builtin_clz, __builtin_ctz
and __builtin_popcount.

To solve this, the patch introduces the following changes based on
Jeff's suggestions:

ext-dce.cc: Extract the redundant sign extension check into a new helper
function is_trivially_redundant_extension. This uses num_sign_bit_copies
evaluated in the outer mode to check if the extension is already redundant,
which allows combine to eliminate it instead of ext-dce leaving SUBREGs
that are harder to optimize.

rtlanal.cc: Improve nonzero_bits1 so that CLZ and CTZ are handled when
the operand mode differs from MODE, as long as it is a scalar integer
mode, since the result depends on the operand.  If the value at
zero is not defined, the fallback is the same as before.

ASM Before:
clzw a0,a0
andn t0,a0,a1
sext.w a0,t0
ret

ASM After:
clzw  a0,a0
andn  a0,a0,a1
ret

Additionally, this patch includes a new test case gcc.target/riscv/pr123905.c
which covers several scenarios: AND, ANDN, and combinations like clz & ctz
and clz & ctz & popcount.

Changes since v4:

-Eliminated the redundant num_sign_bit_copies1 handling.
-Removed the POPCOUNT change from nonzero_bits1.
-nonzero_bits1 keeps the old fallback for CLZ/CTZ, but not for
 mismatched modes, since the result depends on the operand.

Bootstrapped and regression tested on x86_64.
Regression tested on riscv64.

	PR rtl-optimization/123905

	* rtlanal.cc (nonzero_bits1): Improve CLZ and CTZ handling.

update.title: [RISC-V] Fix long branch sequences for Andes extensions
update.body:
LLM review of andes.md turned up numerous problems.  I'm not going to spend a
lot of time on them since I don't know the Andes design but I couldn't just let
this one slide by ;-)

The Andes extensions have two additional conditional branch instructions.  One
is a branch-on-bit capability, the other adds the ability to do equality tests
against small constants.

If you look at the long and short versions, you'll see they use the *same*
condition, but the long version really needs the condition inverted since it
does a branch around the long unconditional.  But the inversion step was never
done.

As I noted, I'm not spending meaningful time on Andes and that includes burning
time to set it up as a testsuite target.  So this has only been tested via
inspection.

Assisted-By: Claude for bug discovery.

Pushing to the trunk.

	* config/riscv/andes.md (branch patterns): Invert condition when
	branching around long unconditional branch when short direct
	branch doesn't fit.
	* config/riscv/iterators.md (sc): New iterator, inverted from "cs".
	(any_eq_inv): New iterator, eq->ne and ne->eq mapping.

update.title: [V850] Fix length computation for branches in V850 port
update.body:
Here's another bug caught by the LLM.

In the E3V5 and newer V850 variants, the range of conditional branches extended
from 8 to 17 bits. The conditional branch sequences were updated to account for
that, except they mucked things up on the older targets.

Essentially the output C fragment selects the sequence based on the length of
the insn

2 bytes -- short conditional
4 bytes -- E3V5 long conditional
6 bytes -- short inverted conditional around "jr"

But the length computation just assumed that the long conditional forms were
always available.

It looks like we're testing base, along with the E3V5 variants, so I can only
assume that the assembler isn't strict enough and that it's likely using the
E3V5 instruction, even on base variants.  Similarly for the simulator.  If
either of those were not true, I would expect massive failures from the
testsuite.

Anyway, the fix is simple, verify we have the E3V5 variant or newer in the
length computation before returning "4".

Regression tested on v850e-elf with no regressions or improvements to existing
tests.  I'm still working through RISC-V bugs in that LLM based tester, but I
wanted to see what it would do if I through another port's MD file at it.

Assisted by: Claude for review of v850.md and testcase generation.

gcc/
	* config/v850/v850.md (conditional branch patterns): Fix length
	computation for designs without long conditional branches.

gcc/testsuite
	* gcc.target/v850/min_bit.c: New test.

update.title: [RISC-V] Fix incorrect long branch sequence for Andes and REGNO reference in peephole
update.body:
More LLM discovered issues.  First in andes.md we're trying to emit a
conditional branch around a long branch sequence.  That's usually done by using
a forward label like 0f or 1f.  The output template used %1f, so it's going to
append 'f' to whatever the output string is for operand1. Opps.  That output
template should just use 1f.  There's other problems with the long branch
sequences, but I need to read the Andes manual to make sure I don't muck up the
fix.

Second was a case where we're using REGNO on an object that could be a SUBREG.
It's a pretty low impact peephole, so I've just adjusted the condition to
ensure the operands are REGs.

Tested on riscv64-elf and riscv32-elf.  However, I doubt that really exercises
either of these two paths at all.

	* config/riscv/andes.md (branch-on-bit pattern): Reference the forward
	label correctly in the long branch sequence.
	* config/riscv/peephole.md: Require operands to be a REG before asking
	for the REGNO.

update.title: RISC-V: Use clmulr for reversed crc64 on rv64
update.body:
This removes the guards that disables the clmulr pattern added by
patch r17-4206-ge91f79891fc657: Use clmulr for reversed crc32 on rv32
from being used on rv64.

This changes the calculation of the reflected quotient (on the host) to
fit inside 64 bits. gf2n_poly_long_div_quotient calculates
x^128 / (x^64 + lower order terms) = x^64 + lower order terms.
Meaning the result is missing an implicit 1 in front of the msb.

After reversing, this missing 1 should be after the lsb. This is
re-added with a shift and an or. This causes the msb to fall outside
the result stored in t0.

The value in t0 is only used by the emitted clmul or vclmul
instructions. Clmul only emits the bottom 64 bits, representing x^63 and
lower order terms. This is unaffected by the missing bit that
represents x^64, because it would always fall outside the result.

Regtested on rv32gc, rv32gc_zbc, rv64gc, and rv64gc_zbc.

	Remove 64 bit guard.
	* config/riscv/riscv.cc (riscv_optab_supported_p): Likewise.
	64 bit guard.
	(expand_reversed_crc_using_clmul): Adapt quotient calculation
	for 65 bits.

gcc/testsuite/ChangeLog:

	applied for crc64

update.body:
This is a mis-compile caught by my LLM checker for machine descriptions.

Basically the pattern in question has two operands, one in SI, one in DI that
ultimately refer to the same pseudo register.  The pattern works fine when bits

bits are set.

the benefit of the pattern most of the time which is precisely what this patch
does.

The existing test can't prove the nonzero bits quality we need for 2 of the 24
tests, so the counts are adjusted accordingly.  And an execution test is added
which trips the bug.

update.body:
A few more bitmanip.md fixes for LLM exposed issues.

This patch targets the potential to use an accessor like [U]INTVAL on something
that is not a CONST_INT.  The common case is accepting an immediate_operand,
then checking [U]INTVAL in the insn's condition.  So if the pattern were passed
a CONST node we could either get unexpected results or an ICE.

So instead of immediate_operand, we can use the tighter const_int_operand.
There's a similar kind of case with arith_operand accepting REGs, so requesting
UINTVAL is just bogus.

There was one case of potentially letting a SUBREG through and testing its
REGNO.  This was actually fixed up in the predicate.

Given how obviously wrong these cases were, I didn't ask the LLM to try and
generate tests.  Ideally we squash these out and going forward review catches
them before they get into the tree.

Bootstrapped and regression tested on the k3, c920 and k1.  Also tested on
riscv64-elf and riscv32-elf.  Pushing to the trunk.

gcc/
	* config/riscv/bitmanip.md (shNadduw): Use const_int_operand rather
	than immediate_operand and const_arith_oprerand instead of
	arith_operand.
	(slliuw, bexti): Similarly.
	(bclr splitter with masked position): Similarly.
	* config/riscv/predicates.md (x1x5_operand): Only allow REGs.
update.author: JeffreyALaw

update.title: [PR target/127865][RISC-V] Refine selection of AOP for RISC-V
update.body:
So Anton's test showed a case where we'd have been better off steering towards
PLUS for rv64 that had not occurred to me.

In particular if we steer towards PLUS, then we can get sign extensions for
free via addw/addiw; the sequence doesn't even have to end, they can appear in
the middle of an instruction stream and allow us to eliminate a sign extension
later as evidenced by Anton's test.  So one more reason to steer towards PLUS.

This has the potential to make identification of bseti harder.  We'll have to
monitor that and I wouldn't be surprised if final resolution of an AOP op
really needs to wait until after combine is done.  But that's definitely in the
future work space.

Bootstrapped and regression tested on the k3 and c920.  K1 is in flight.  Also
tested on riscv32-elf and riscv64-elf.  Pushing to the trunk.

Assisted-By: LLM for patch review

	PR target/127865
gcc/
	* config/riscv/riscv.md (aop<mode>3): Steer more operations towards
	PLUS for rv64.

gcc/testsuite

	* gcc.target/riscv/pr127865.c: New test.

update.title: [RISC-V] Fix two RISC-V bitmanip bugs spotted by LLM review
update.body:
First in the recently added pattern which rewrites mask constants in AOP
operations to encourage simplification or elimination of the AND mask, make
sure not to touch the SI sign bit.

We're taking an and+bclr+addiw sequence and turning it into bclr+ior.  The
former sign extends its result from bit 31 into bits 32..63, the latter
sequence does not.  The pattern is guarded on knowing we have 33+ sign bit
copies in the nonconstant operand.  What I missed was ensuring that the bit
twiddle doesn't change the SI sign bit or any copies of the sign bit.

The second case rewrites a slli+zext+shNadd into slli+shNadd.uw.   It's similar
to the slli+slliw pattern elsewhere in bitmanip.md. If we're not careful we can
generate a negative shift count.  I don't think we're seeing that in practice
as the constants which generate that scenario bump the cost and we don't apply
the transformation.  But it's better to fix the pattern so that it works
properly in case we fix the cost (which Shreya is working on).

Both fixes have been bootstrapped and regression tested on the k3.  The c920
wedged up again (common) and the k1 is queued waiting for a prior job to
finish.  Also tested on riscv32-elf and riscv64-elf.  Pushing to the trunk.

Assisted-By: LLM for bug hunting in bitmanip.md and review of my patch.

gcc/
	* config/riscv/bitmanip.md (shift_then_shNadd.uw): Ensure popcount of
	mask is < 32.
	(and+bclr+addiw -> bclr+ior splitter): Ensure the operation preserves
	the SI mode sign extension to DI.
update.author: JeffreyALaw
